results.title: Four isotypic components in a tensor square for a simple group of order 10200960
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a finite simple group $G$ of order $10200960$ and an irreducible complex representation $\rho$ of $G$ on a vector space $V$ of dimension $22$ such that the tensor square $V \otimes V$, regarded as a module over the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$ through the diagonal action $g \mapsto \rho(g) \otimes \rho(g)$, has exactly $4$ isotypic components.

results.title: Supersoluble group (Kourovka 15.81)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble when it has a series $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$ of subgroups, each normal in $G$, such that every factor $H_{i+1}/H_i$ is cyclic.

results.title: Uncomplemented maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups (Kourovka 15.81, Skiba)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that every finite group $G$ that is not supersoluble has, for some prime $p$, a non-cyclic Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ with a maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ that has no proper complement in $G$, that is, there is no subgroup $K \ne G$ with $MK = G$ and $M \cap K = 1$.

results.title: Finite non-supersoluble groups have uncomplemented maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite group $G$ that is not supersoluble, there are a prime $p$ and a non-cyclic Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$ with a maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ that has no proper complement in $G$: there is no subgroup $K \ne G$ with $MK = G$ and $M \cap K = 1$. This answers Kourovka Problem 15.81 in the affirmative.

results.title: Shortest elements of normal closures in free groups (Kourovka 11.82, Remeslennikov)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every free group $F$ and every $r \ne 1$ in $F$, if $s$ is a nontrivial element of the normal closure $R$ of $r$ in $F$ whose reduced word length is minimal among the nontrivial elements of $R$, then $s$ is conjugate to $r$, to $r^{-1}$, or, for some $f \in F$, to $[r, f] = r^{-1} f^{-1} r f$ or to $[r^{-1}, f] = r f^{-1} r^{-1} f$.

results.title: Negative answer to Kourovka 11.82 on shortest elements of normal closures

results.title: Maschke's theorem
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Unitary divisors of a prime power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every prime $p$ and every natural number $m$, the unitary divisors of $p^m$, that is, the divisors $d$ of $p^m$ with $\gcd(d, p^m/d) = 1$, are exactly $1$ and $p^m$.

results.title: Products of unitary divisors of coprime numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be coprime natural numbers. If $a$ is a unitary divisor of $m$ and $b$ is a unitary divisor of $n$, then $ab$ is a unitary divisor of $mn$.

results.title: Gcd with a coprime factor preserves unitary divisors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be coprime natural numbers. If $d$ is a unitary divisor of $mn$, then $\gcd(d, m)$ is a unitary divisor of $m$.

results.title: The arithmetic function $c^{\Omega}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a monoid with zero and let $c \in R$. This is the arithmetic function $c^{\Omega}$ with values in $R$ given by $c^{\Omega}(0) = 0$ and $c^{\Omega}(n) = c^{\Omega(n)}$ for $n \ge 1$, where $\Omega(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. It is completely multiplicative.

results.title: Value of $c^{\Omega}$ at a positive integer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a monoid with zero, let $c \in R$, and let $c^{\Omega}$ be the arithmetic function with values in $R$ that is $0$ at $0$ and $c^{\Omega(n)}$ at each $n \ge 1$, where $\Omega(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. For every natural number $n \ne 0$, its value at $n$ is $c^{\Omega(n)}$.

results.title: Complete multiplicativity of $c^{\Omega}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a monoid with zero and $c \in R$. Let $c^{\Omega}$ be the arithmetic function $n \mapsto c^{\Omega(n)}$ for $n \ge 1$, where $\Omega(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. Then $c^{\Omega}$ is completely multiplicative: for all natural numbers $m$ and $n$, its value at $mn$ is the product of its values at $m$ and at $n$.

results.title: Multiplicativity of $c^{\Omega}$
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Unitary convolution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring. The unitary convolution of two arithmetic functions $f$ and $g$ with values in $R$ is the arithmetic function $f \sqcup g$ given by $(f \sqcup g)(n) = \sum_{d \parallel n} f(d)\, g(n/d)$, where the sum runs over the unitary divisors $d$ of $n$: for $n \ge 1$ these are the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $\gcd(d, n/d) = 1$, and $0$ has no unitary divisors. In particular $(f \sqcup g)(0) = 0$.

results.title: Unitary convolution as a sum over unitary divisors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $f$ and $g$ be arithmetic functions with values in $R$. For every natural number $n$, their unitary convolution $f \sqcup g$ satisfies $(f \sqcup g)(n) = \sum_{d \parallel n} f(d)\, g(n/d)$, where the sum runs over the unitary divisors $d$ of $n$: for $n \ge 1$ these are the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $\gcd(d, n/d) = 1$, and for $n = 0$ there are none, so the sum is $0$.

results.title: Unitary convolution at $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $f$ and $g$ be arithmetic functions with values in $R$. Their unitary convolution $f \sqcup g$, defined by $(f \sqcup g)(n) = \sum_{d \parallel n} f(d)\, g(n/d)$ over the unitary divisors $d$ of $n$, satisfies $(f \sqcup g)(1) = f(1)\, g(1)$.

results.title: Unitary convolution at prime powers
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: The unitary convolution of multiplicative functions is multiplicative

results.summary: Let $X$ be a second-countable topological space, $Y$ a measurable space with a measure $\mu$, $f : X \to Y$ a function and $s \subseteq X$. If every point $x \in s$ has a neighbourhood $V$ with $\mu(f(V \cap s)) = 0$, then $\mu(f(s)) = 0$.

results.title: The graph of a measurable function is a null set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \ge 0$ be an integer and let $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be Borel measurable. Identify $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}$ with $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ by taking the last coordinate as $y$. Then the graph $\Gamma = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R} : y = f(x)\}$ is a Borel measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ and has Lebesgue measure $0$.

results.title: Bias of an estimator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $S$ be a measurable space, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator, $\mu$ a probability measure on $S$ for which $W$ is integrable, and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ a target. The bias of $W$ under $\mu$ at $\theta$ is $\int_S W \, d\mu - \theta$, the expected value of $W$ under $\mu$ minus $\theta$.

results.title: Bias as an integral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a measurable space, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator, $\mu$ a probability measure on $S$ for which $W$ is integrable, and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ a target. Then the bias of $W$ under $\mu$ at $\theta$ equals $\int_S W \, d\mu - \theta$.

results.title: Mean squared error
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be an estimator and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ a target value, and suppose the squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is $\mu$-integrable. The mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ is the real number $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$.

results.title: Mean squared error as an integral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and suppose the squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is $\mu$-integrable. Then the mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ equals $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$.

results.title: Extended mean squared error
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be an estimator and let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ be a target value. The extended mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ is the (lower) Lebesgue integral $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ of the nonnegative squared error, computed in $[0, \infty]$. It is defined for every $W$, with no integrability hypothesis.

results.title: Finite and extended mean squared error agree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and suppose the squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is $\mu$-integrable. Then the extended mean squared error $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$, computed in $[0, \infty]$, is finite and equals the mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$.

results.title: Extended mean squared error of a measurable non-integrable squared error is infinite

results.title: Legendre transform
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$, give $\mathbb{R}^d$ its standard inner product, and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$. The Legendre transform of $\Lambda$ at $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is the Fenchel conjugate of $\Lambda$ at the linear functional $y \mapsto \langle x, y \rangle$, that is, the extended real number $\Lambda^*(x) = \sup_{y \in \mathbb{R}^d} \big(\langle x, y \rangle - \Lambda(y)\big)$.

results.title: Supremum formula for the Legendre transform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$. For every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$ of $\Lambda$ satisfies $\Lambda^*(x) = \sup_{l \in \mathbb{R}^d} \big(\langle l, x \rangle - \Lambda(l)\big)$.

results.title: Fenchel–Young inequality for the Legendre transform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$, with Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$. For all $x, l \in \mathbb{R}^d$, we have $\langle l, x \rangle - \Lambda(l) \le \Lambda^*(x)$ in $[-\infty, \infty]$.

results.title: The Legendre transform is order-reversing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2 : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$, with Legendre transforms $\Lambda_1^*$ and $\Lambda_2^*$. If $\Lambda_1(y) \le \Lambda_2(y)$ for every $y \in \mathbb{R}^d$, then $\Lambda_2^*(x) \le \Lambda_1^*(x)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

results.title: The epigraph of the Legendre transform is convex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$, with Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$. Then the set $\{(x, t) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R} : \Lambda^*(x) \le t\}$ is convex.

results.title: A finite Legendre transform is convex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$, with Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$. If $\Lambda^*(x)$ is a real number for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, then $\Lambda^*$, viewed as a function $\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$, is convex on $\mathbb{R}^d$.

results.title: The double Legendre transform lies below the function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be a function that never takes the value $-\infty$, with Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$. Then the Legendre transform $\Lambda^{**}$ of $\Lambda^*$ satisfies $\Lambda^{**}(x) \le \Lambda(x)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

results.title: The half squared norm is its own Legendre transform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $q : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be $q(y) = \|y\|^2 / 2$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean norm. Its Legendre transform $q^*$ satisfies $q^*(x) = \|x\|^2 / 2$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$; in particular every value of $q^*$ is finite.

results.title: Legendre transform of the zero function at the origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be the zero function. Its Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$ satisfies $\Lambda^*(0) = 0$.

results.title: Legendre transform of the zero function away from the origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be the zero function. Its Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$ satisfies $\Lambda^*(x) = +\infty$ for every nonzero $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

results.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $c$ be a list of $k$ distinct pages and let $f$ be any list of requests. Then the search through $c$ for the first page that does not occur among the first $k - 1$ entries of $f$ succeeds; in particular, some page of $c$ does not occur there.

results.title: Each offline step is a legal transition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $c$ be a cache of at most $k$ distinct pages, let $p$ be a requested page and let $f$ be the list of future requests. Then the event and the new cache produced by the offline step with cache size $k$ on $c$, $p$ and $f$ form a legal transition from $c$ of the caching system with capacity $k$.

results.title: The offline trace is legal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $c$ be a cache of at most $k$ distinct pages and let $\sigma$ be a list of requests. Then the offline trace with cache size $k$ from $c$ on $\sigma$ is a legal run of the caching system with capacity $k$ from $c$ to some final cache, and the pages served by its events are, in order, exactly $\sigma$.

results.title: Hits do not change the offline strategy's misses
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, let $c$ be a cache and let $w$ be a request sequence all of whose requests lie in $c$. Then for every request sequence $\tau$, the offline strategy with capacity $k$ (on a miss with a full cache, evict the first cached page not among the next $k - 1$ requests, if there is one) started with cache $c$ misses as many times on $w$ followed by $\tau$ as on $\tau$ alone.

results.title: After a miss on a full cache, every page except the evicted one is present
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a list of $k$ distinct pages among the $k + 1$ pages $0, \dots, k$, let $p$ be a page not in $c$, and let $v$ be any page. Then every page $x \neq v$ lies in the cache obtained from $c$ by removing $v$ and adding $p$.

results.title: Misses of a paging policy on list caches
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let a paging policy be given by its step function, which maps a cache (a list of pages) and a requested page to the next cache. Starting from a cache $c$, the policy serves a request sequence $p_1, \dots, p_n$ by setting $c_0 = c$ and $c_i = \mathrm{step}(c_{i-1}, p_i)$ for each $i$; its number of misses is the number of indices $i$ with $p_i \notin c_{i-1}$.

results.title: LRU as a policy on list caches
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every capacity $k$, the misses of the paging policy whose step is the LRU step with capacity $k$ coincide with the LRU misses with capacity $k$, from every starting cache and on every request sequence.

results.title: One step of FIFO paging
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The cache is a list of pages, oldest first, and $k$ is the capacity. On a request for a page $p$ already in the cache $c$, the cache stays $c$. Otherwise $p$ is appended at the back of $c$; if $c$ had fewer than $k$ pages, that is the new cache, and if not, the front page, the one loaded earliest, is removed as well.

results.title: One FIFO step keeps the cache legal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a list $c$ of pages has no duplicates and at most $k$ entries, then for every page $p$ the cache produced from $c$ by one FIFO step with capacity $k$ on request $p$ also has no duplicates and at most $k$ entries.

results.title: Legal cache
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ of pages and a capacity $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a legal cache is a list of pages of $\alpha$ with no duplicates and at most $k$ entries.

results.title: FIFO keeps the cache legal on every request sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a list $c$ of pages has no duplicates and at most $k$ entries, then for every finite request sequence $\sigma$ the cache obtained from $c$ by serving the requests of $\sigma$ in order, each with one FIFO step of capacity $k$, also has no duplicates and at most $k$ entries.

results.title: FIFO paging as an online pager
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The online pager with capacity $k$ whose states are the legal caches of capacity $k$ (lists of at most $k$ distinct pages, oldest first), whose initial state is the empty cache, whose cache in a state is that list itself, and which serves a request $p$ by one FIFO step with capacity $k$.

results.title: FIFO as an online pager misses as often as the FIFO step policy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every legal cache $q$ of capacity $k$ (at most $k$ distinct pages) and every request sequence $\sigma$, the number of misses of the FIFO online pager started in $q$ and serving $\sigma$ equals the number of misses of the policy given by the FIFO step with capacity $k$ serving $\sigma$ from the cache $q$.

results.title: FIFO is `k`-competitive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: FIFO is `k`-competitive (Sleator and Tarjan). Let $k \ge 1$, and let $\tau$ be a legal trace of the caching system with capacity $k$ that starts from a cache $c_0$ of at most $k$ distinct pages; let $m$ be its number of misses. Then the FIFO online pager with capacity $k$, started in any legal cache (at most $k$ distinct pages) and serving the requests of $\tau$ in order, misses at most $k m + k$ times.

results.title: FIFO is `k`-competitive against the offline optimum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $\sigma$ be a finite request sequence, and let $c_0$ be a list of at most $k$ distinct pages. Let $m$ be the number of misses of the furthest-in-future manager with capacity $k$ serving $\sigma$ from the cache $c_0$. Then the FIFO online pager with capacity $k$, started in any legal cache (at most $k$ distinct pages), misses at most $k m + k$ of the requests of $\sigma$.
